comparator.name: Law
comparator.institution: Erasmus School of Law, Erasmus University Rotterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the current 2026-2027 public curriculum and current Osiris course records. The programme is a fixed 180-EC Dutch-law bachelor organised as three 60-EC years. Years 1 and 2 each contain eight substantive legal or contextual courses plus a year-long legal-academic-skills component. Year 3 contains a 15-EC minor, 7 EC of Public International Law, 7 EC of Legal Philosophy, a 21-EC Law & Business block, and a 10-EC legal-academic-skills component that includes the bachelor thesis. The programme page supplies the current course sequence and descriptions; the linked current Osiris records supply the credit weights.

candidates.label: Private law, business and commercial relationships

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic law, legal-reasoning, law-and-society and criminal-law interests. Two further generator-backed directions remain especially coherent at UCR: public, international and European law; and private law, business and commercial relationships. Both are feasible and qualitatively distinct. The closest match and public route differ by six courses, the closest match and private/business route differ by eleven, and the two related routes differ by twelve. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached.

alternatives.label: Law, politics & society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains UCR’s full available law sequence and embeds it in political science, sociology, economics, philosophy, research and communication. The label states the actual interdisciplinary composition and does not imply a Dutch qualifying law degree.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines broad legal foundations and human rights with criminal, private, constitutional, international and EU law, supported by politics, sociology, economics, ethics, empirical research and persuasive communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every advanced law course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected economics courses with that prerequisite. Introductory politics, sociology, economics and ethics precede advanced EU politics, social theory, public economics, conflict study and research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Public, international & European law
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum concentrates constitutional and international law, EU law and politics, comparative institutions, conflict, empire and social movements. The label names that public and cross-border focus without implying a complete Dutch-law curriculum.
alternatives.concept: A public and cross-border legal direction connecting constitutional, international and EU law with comparative politics, international relations, EU institutions, conflict, history, sociology, public economics and qualitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal and private law, political philosophy, ethics, persuasive communication and negotiation. It adds business foundations, modern and imperial history, the history of warfare, international business governance and social-movement study. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising emphasis shifts to public institutions, cross-border orders and their historical and social contexts.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes constitutional, international and EU law. Comparative politics, international-relations theory, sociology, economics and research methods precede advanced EU politics, conflict, social theory, international governance and historical research. Business Foundations precedes International Business & Governance. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Private law, business & commercial relations
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines private and transnational business law with accounting, finance, economics, strategy, international business, organisational behaviour, negotiation, research and communication. The label reflects those available fields without overstating UCR’s private-law depth.
alternatives.concept: A private and commercial legal direction combining private, international, constitutional and EU law with transnational business law, accounting, finance, economics, strategy, organisational behaviour, negotiation and applied business research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, political philosophy, comparative politics, international-relations theory, EU politics, conflict studies, qualitative sociology and historical research. It adds business foundations, accounting and finance, digital strategy, organisational psychology, transnational business law, international business governance, econometrics and market research. Eleven courses differ from the closest match and twelve differ from the public/international route.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Business Foundations establish the legal and commercial strands before advanced private, EU, transnational-business and international-governance courses. Research Methods & Statistics precedes negotiation, public economics, econometrics and market research. The final year concentrates private law, international business, social theory, advanced communication, finance, econometrics and applied research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

blocks: Both introduce legal systems, sources, fields and the social operation of law; UCR does so comparatively rather than through a Dutch doctrinal sequence.
Both examine constitutional and administrative institutions, public powers, legal limits and protected rights; UCR compares systems rather than teaching Dutch doctrine.
UCR has separate public-international-law and EU-law courses, but each is aligned to the comparator’s later dedicated component; it has no additional introductory combined course.
Comparative Constitutional Law already aligns to the comparator’s first-year combined state and administrative-law foundation; UCR has no second dedicated constitutional-law course.
Comparative Constitutional Law includes administrative-law foundations but UCR has no separate advanced Dutch administrative-law course.
Both introduce private-law rights and obligations; UCR surveys property, contract, family and related relationships rather than a Dutch doctrinal sequence.
Both introduce substantive criminal-law reasoning and criminal justice, including accountability and safeguards.
UCR Principles of Private Law includes contract and obligations but is already aligned to the introductory private-law component; there is no second dedicated obligations course.
UCR surveys property law but does not provide the comparator’s dedicated property-rights and insolvency sequence.
UCR has no dedicated course in Dutch civil procedure or enforcement.
UCR Criminal Law & Criminal Justice discusses procedure and safeguards but does not reproduce a dedicated Dutch criminal-procedure course.
UCR Criminal Law & Criminal Justice is already aligned to the introductory criminal-law component and does not form a second advanced Dutch-doctrine course.

Both apply legal reasoning to business relationships; UCR concentrates on transnational contracts, trade, investment and commercial disputes rather than the comparator’s integrated Dutch Law & Business project.
Both situate legal rules in their economic and social context; UCR supplies the economics foundation directly.
UCR Public Economics analyses taxation economically but does not teach Dutch tax-law doctrine, sources, assessment or procedure.
Both support empirical study of institutions and social outcomes; UCR provides general research design and statistics rather than a law-specific empirical course.
Both develop argument, writing and oral presentation; UCR teaches these through rhetoric rather than Dutch legal documents.
Both advance argument and communication, while UCR focuses on persuasion and framing rather than a year-long legal-skills sequence.

The comparator requires advanced legal-academic skills and an independent bachelor thesis. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so the component remains unmatched and UCR’s optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.
The comparator’s 15-EC minor is open choice space. UCR flexibility is distributed across the whole 180-EC plan, so no single scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme is a professional academic Dutch-law degree with a continuous jurisdiction-specific sequence in private law, obligations, property and insolvency, civil procedure, constitutional and administrative law, substantive and procedural criminal law, EU and international law, legal-academic skills, applied Law & Business work and a bachelor thesis. UCR offers an interdisciplinary law cluster and related politics, sociology, economics, business, history, philosophy and research courses. It does not reproduce the Dutch doctrinal sequence, dedicated procedural subjects, year-long legal-skills training or professional qualification path. These pathways therefore compare related legal and institutional fields; none is a substitute for the external law degree.
